correctness.rationale: For every realization, the Rogers dual certificate at \(\eta=1/t\) equals \(|B|+(s-S_B)/t\). Rewriting \(N\) as \(S_A/t+\sum_{i\in A}(1-X_i/t)\) and subtracting yields exactly the unused-budget term plus the two one-sided threshold-disagreement sums, which combine to \(\sum_{i\in A	riangle B}|X_i-t|\). Both are nonnegative. The BRS threshold equation makes \(\mathbb ES_B=s\), and absolute continuity gives \(\mathbb E|B|=\sum_iF_i(t)\), proving the expected identity. Equality of expectations forces the nonnegative pointwise defect to vanish almost surely, equivalently \(S_B=s\) almost surely. The exact-rational verifier independently replays the pathwise algebra over a large finite grid.

value.rationale: The BRS inequality is a standard dependence-free packing bound, and the closest survey explicitly develops refinements. The new identity resolves all slack in the canonical optimized threshold certificate into two mathematically interpretable parts: unused budget and threshold-set mismatch. It strictly refines the published residual correction whenever those sets disagree, gives a clean iff equality criterion, and immediately proves strictness for independent nondegenerate truncated coordinates. This is a structural statement about the inequality rather than a numerical example or parameter substitution.
